children: Lakdhanavi Limited, a power company from Sri Lanka, has secured a turnkey deal valued at roughly LKR25bn ($75mn) to construct a natural gas-fired plant with 57 MW of capacity in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands of India, according to a November 15 report by

The deal is the company's first in India's market for power plant engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) work. Economic ties between the two neighbours are usually framed around Indian investment, aid and infrastructure involvement in Sri Lanka. The award shows business can also flow from Sri Lanka into India, according to the report.

Lakdhanavi was the lowest-priced bidder in an international tender run by NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Limited (NVVN). NVVN is fully owned by India's state-controlled National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited.

The two sides signed the agreement on September 21 at the NTPC Office Complex in Noida. Senior representatives of NVVN, Lakdhanavi and parent company LTL Holdings attended. They also discussed how the project would be carried out and possible cooperation in future.

Located in Hope Town, Port Blair, on the island of Andaman, the facility aims to strengthen local electricity supply and, by way of liquefied natural gas infrastructure, underpin energy security over the long term.
Lakdhanavi's own engineers will execute the project, and Finland's Wärtsilä Corporation will provide the generating equipment.

LTL Holdings established Lakdhanavi as an arm of the group toward the end of the 1990s. Lakdhanavi is an independent power producer that also supplies operations and maintenance services to thermal and renewable projects, and its earlier power work has taken it to Bangladesh, Nepal and the Maldives.

LTL Group, whose interests cover power generation as well as transmission and distribution, ranks as the largest player in Sri Lanka's electricity sector. Its origins lie in a joint venture formed by a European firm and the Ceylon Electricity Board. National Transmission Network System Provider (Pvt) Ltd, a state entity that falls under the Ministry of Energy, currently holds a 35% stake in LTL Holdings.

Energy Minister Anura Karunathilake met LTL management and told them the government was pleased that a Sri Lankan company had won a major infrastructure contract in a market as large and competitive as India.

Describing the award as a milestone both for Lakdhanavi and for engineering in Sri Lanka, Nuhuman Marikkar, who serves as chief executive of Lakdhanavi as well as LTL Holdings, said the contract demonstrated the company's strong technical capabilities and the dedication of its employees. Lakdhanavi, he said, was eager to collaborate closely with NVVN on delivering the plant.

title: Sri Lanka's Lakdhanavi to build gas power plant in India
